missing_dependency: an accepted executable route issuing a mandate-scoped representative session
frontend_behaviour: The workspace starts in the anonymous state, states that mandate sessions cannot be established against any accepted runtime, and offers no credential entry that would imply otherwise.

missing_dependency: an accepted mandate register exposing the mandate, its level, and its active authority window
frontend_behaviour: Scope is never resolved from the network. Every protected surface refuses with scope_mismatch or unavailable and names the missing register.

missing_dependency: an accepted server-side authority check evaluated at commit time
frontend_behaviour: No action that would require commit-time revalidation is offered as executable. The requirement is displayed, not simulated.

missing_dependency: an accepted executable step-up ceremony returning a raised assurance level
frontend_behaviour: Surfaces that require step-up render the step_up_required state with the reason, and the trigger is inert by construction rather than disabled by styling.

missing_dependency: an accepted executable route listing mandate-scoped citizen cases
frontend_behaviour: The desk renders the unavailable state with the named dependency. No placeholder case list is shown, because a fabricated list is indistinguishable from a real one to the user.

missing_dependency: an accepted executable route returning a single case within mandate scope
frontend_behaviour: Detail routes refuse non-disclosingly: the refusal is identical whether the case does not exist or lies outside scope.

missing_dependency: an accepted executable case assignment operation
frontend_behaviour: The action is described in the action register with its authority requirement and reported as blocked. It is never offered as executable.

missing_dependency: an accepted executable state-transition operation with optimistic-concurrency semantics
frontend_behaviour: Transitions are not attempted. The state machine models the safe outcomes, including the uncertain outcome, and is exercised only under the governed test profile.

missing_dependency: an accepted executable route recording an outbound response against a case
frontend_behaviour: Composition surfaces are not presented as a send path. Nothing composed is described as delivered.

missing_dependency: an accepted executable search operation that is server-side scope-bound
frontend_behaviour: Search is unavailable. The interface never offers an unscoped search field, so there is no surface on which a cross-mandate query could be typed.

missing_dependency: an accepted executable route returning stored position drafts
frontend_behaviour: The position surface renders unavailable rather than an empty list, because an empty list asserts that nothing exists.

missing_dependency: an accepted executable route persisting a draft
frontend_behaviour: A draft composed in this workspace exists only in volatile memory for the life of the surface. It is labelled as unsaved, and no browser storage receives it.

missing_dependency: an accepted executable route accepting an internal submission
frontend_behaviour: Submission is reported blocked with the named dependency. The workspace never reports a draft as submitted.

missing_dependency: an accepted executable route returning deviation records with provenance
frontend_behaviour: Unavailable state with the named dependency.

missing_dependency: an accepted executable route recording a deviation against a governed decision
frontend_behaviour: The composition surface exists and enforces the record's shape locally, including the requirement that a deviation references a decision and cannot alter it. Nothing is transmitted.

missing_dependency: an accepted executable route resolving a governed decision identifier to its published record
frontend_behaviour: References are accepted as opaque text and explicitly marked unverified. The workspace does not claim a reference is valid.

missing_dependency: an accepted executable route returning a representative's own declarations
frontend_behaviour: Unavailable state with the named dependency.

missing_dependency: an accepted executable route accepting a declaration submission
frontend_behaviour: The form validates locally and reports the submission blocked. It never reports acceptance, and it never asserts a compliance obligation has been met.

missing_dependency: a server-authoritative proposal and authorization contract: a proposal state distinct from PUBLISHED, and an authorization decided by the server rather than asserted by the caller
frontend_behaviour: The workspace offers proposal composition only, states in the interface that a proposal is not an approval, and reports submission blocked. It never sets, sends or relies on an authorization flag of its own.
security_finding: A caller-supplied actor_is_authorized boolean is a self-asserted authorization: the caller declares its own permission and the service accepts the declaration. FRONT-05 must not treat it as evidence that any authorization occurred, and must not build a privileged path on it â doing so would let a proposal reach publication carrying nothing but the proposer's own claim of being allowed to publish. This is a defect in the dependency, not a gap in it: the capability stays blocked until a server-authoritative authorization contract exists, and would remain blocked even if a proposal route were added while the boolean stayed.

missing_dependency: a route returning a publication state whose approval was decided by an authority other than the proposer
frontend_behaviour: Publication state is shown as unknown rather than assumed, and an approved state is presented as public only when a deciding authority and a public rendition reference are both present.
security_finding: An observed publication state carries no independent evidence of who approved it, because the service records no deciding authority. A state read back from such a service cannot distinguish an approval by the publication authority from one the proposer asserted about itself, so this workspace treats an approved state with no recorded decider as not public â see mayPresentAsPublic in domain/publication.ts.

missing_dependency: an accepted executable route returning active conflict restrictions for a mandate
frontend_behaviour: Restrictions cannot be read, so the workspace fails closed: it neither asserts that a restriction is absent nor treats an unknown restriction as cleared.

missing_dependency: not applicable â the capability is prohibited for this workspace, not merely blocked
frontend_behaviour: No surface, no action descriptor, and no port exists. The prohibition is enforced by absence and asserted by a total function returning false.

missing_dependency: an accepted executable read route over a protected register
frontend_behaviour: Registry-derived facts are shown as unavailable. No registry mutation surface exists at all.

missing_dependency: an accepted executable route returning a decided eligibility status
frontend_behaviour: Eligibility is displayed as undetermined-elsewhere, with the explicit statement that this workspace does not decide it.

missing_dependency: any control-plane implementation whatsoever
frontend_behaviour: The workspace states that its own actions are not currently audited by an accepted control plane, which is a limitation the operator must know.

missing_dependency: a connected accepted telemetry platform
frontend_behaviour: No telemetry leaves the browser. The validator asserts the allowlist is enforced and that case content can never enter an event.
Every refusal kind renders a safe message, a committed/not-committed/unknown statement, and one safe next action, with non-disclosure preserved where required.
There is no representation of an unbounded scope in the type system, so a cross-mandate request has no expressible form.
Each blocked surface names the offline route that remains valid, so no citizen matter is dropped because the software is unfinished.
